statement: The relationship between the Holy Roman Empire and the papacy was the defining tension of medieval European politics, oscillating between cooperation (the Ottonian-Gregorian partnership of the 10th century), conflict (the Investiture Controversy, 1076–1122), renewed cooperation (the Crusades), and catastrophic conflict (Frederick II vs. Innocent IV, 1239–1250). The fundamental question — who held ultimate authority in Christendom, the pope or the emperor — was never definitively resolved. The papacy's greatest victories (deposing Henry IV in 1076, deposing Frederick II in 1245) were matched by the empire's resilience and eventual institutional independence.
